Title and Summary
Director, SME Global Market Expansion
Director, SME Global Market Expansion
Overview
The Director, SME Global Market Expansion will lead Mastercard’s global market expansion strategy for SMEs, owning a portfolio of growth initiatives with direct accountability for Gross Dollar Volume (GDV), Net Revenue (NR), market share expansion, and pipeline creation. This role combines strategic leadership, commercial execution, and ecosystem development to create scalable growth engines across priority markets and channels. The Director will partner closely with regional leadership, Product, Finance, Franchise, Marketing, and Sales teams to identify whitespace opportunities, shape investment priorities, and accelerate growth at scale.
Role
Define and lead Mastercard's global SME market expansion strategy, identifying the highest-value opportunities to accelerate card displacement and capture incremental payment flows across priority markets.
Own a portfolio of growth initiatives with direct accountability for GDV growth, Net Revenue generation, market penetration, and pipeline development.
Establish the strategic framework for identifying target geographies, SME segments, verticals, and use cases with the greatest commercial potential.
Lead the development and execution of global growth programs that accelerate the migration from cash, checks, wires, and alternative payment methods to Mastercard solutions.
Influence investment decisions and strategic priorities by building executive-level business cases and commercialization plans.
Serve as the executive sponsor for critical growth initiatives, ensuring successful execution from opportunity identification through scaling and market adoption.
Key Responsibilities
Strategy Development & Commercial Leadership
Define and execute Mastercard's global SME market expansion strategy with accountability for enterprise-level GDV, revenue, and pipeline outcomes.
Develop multi-year growth plans and investment priorities aligned to Mastercard's broader SME growth agenda.
Build and maintain executive-level business cases that quantify financial impact, customer value, and strategic importance.
Prioritize initiatives, investments, and resources based on revenue potential, scalability, competitive advantage, and strategic fit.
Establish growth targets, operating metrics, and performance expectations across markets and regions.
Growth Execution & Scale
Lead large-scale growth initiatives from concept through commercialization and global deployment.
Oversee pilot programs, experimentation frameworks, and test-and-learn methodologies to validate new growth opportunities.
Establish KPI frameworks and governance mechanisms to measure business impact and ensure accountability.
Drive rapid scaling of successful initiatives across multiple geographies while capturing and applying best practices.
Ensure disciplined execution and measurable business outcomes across the expansion portfolio.
Market, Competitive & Customer Intelligence
Lead the development of strategic market insights to identify whitespace opportunities and emerging growth trends.
Analyze payment behaviors, barriers to adoption, and switching dynamics across SME customer segments.
Monitor competitive activity, fintech innovation, embedded finance models, and alternative payment ecosystems to inform strategic decisions.
Translate market intelligence into actionable growth strategies and investment recommendations for senior leadership.
Opportunity Identification & Portfolio Development
Identify high-value payment flows, underserved segments, and new use cases with significant card conversion potential.
Develop prioritization frameworks to guide investment allocation across regions, segments, and initiatives.
Evaluate new business models, partnerships, and distribution channels that accelerate market penetration and revenue growth.
Shape Mastercard's expansion strategy across emerging SME ecosystems, including embedded finance, digital platforms, marketplaces, trade and logistics, and industry-specific verticals.
Cross-Functional & Executive Leadership
Serve as the strategic link between Global SME Product, Regional Product, Franchise, Sales, Marketing, Finance, and Strategy teams.
Drive organizational alignment around growth priorities, resource allocation, and commercialization plans.
Present growth strategies, investment cases, and performance updates to SVP, EVP, and executive leadership audiences.
Influence enterprise-wide decisions through data-driven storytelling and executive stakeholder management.
Strategic Partnerships & Ecosystem Development
Identify, evaluate, and cultivate strategic partnerships that accelerate SME payment adoption and market expansion.
Sponsor initiatives with issuers, fintechs, acquirers, ISVs, platforms, marketplaces, and ecosystem partners.
Develop scalable channel strategies that unlock new customer acquisition opportunities and increase payment volume.
Drive innovative partnership models that extend Mastercard's reach into emerging SME payment ecosystems.
Value Proposition & Commercial Innovation
Shape differentiated SME value propositions that address customer pain points and accelerate payment conversion.
Lead the design and commercialization of new growth initiatives, distribution models, and customer engagement strategies.
Partner with Product and Data & Services teams to embed analytics, insights, and value-added capabilities into market expansion initiatives.
Ensure all initiatives are tied to measurable business impact and scalable commercial outcomes.
All About You
Strategic growth leader with deep experience driving commercial outcomes in payments, fintech, banking, consulting, or financial services.
Proven track record of owning and delivering against significant revenue, GDV, market share, or pipeline objectives.
Strong understanding of SME payment ecosystems, commercial card economics, embedded finance, and payment digitization trends.
Demonstrated ability to identify market opportunities, build business cases, and scale initiatives across multiple regions.
Exceptional executive presence with experience influencing senior leaders and presenting to C-suite stakeholders.
Strong analytical and strategic problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex data into actionable growth strategies.
Entrepreneurial mindset with a history of building new capabilities, launching growth programs, and driving organizational change.
Ability to operate effectively in highly matrixed global organizations and lead through influence.
Results-oriented leader with a strong bias for action, accountability, and business impact.
Qualifications
Required
12+ years of experience in strategy, payments, product management, commercial leadership, consulting, fintech, or related industries.
Proven experience leading growth strategies and commercial initiatives with measurable financial outcomes.
Experience managing complex, cross-functional programs across multiple geographies and stakeholders.
Strong financial acumen with experience building business cases, investment frameworks, and growth models.
Corporate Security Responsibility
All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

jd.text:
Our Purpose
Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. Title and Summary
Manager, Localization & Transformation, Mastercard Strategic Growth
About the Team
The global payments landscape is undergoing rapid and structural change, driven by geopolitical fragmentation, regulatory activism, and the rise of sovereign digital infrastructure. Governments are playing an increasingly active role in shaping domestic payments ecosystems, redefining competitive dynamics and creating both risk and opportunity for global networks like Mastercard.
The Localization & Transformation team exists in response to this environment. We drive Mastercard’s enterprise-wide commitment to showing up locally and winning domestically (“Domestic Relevance”), ensuring our strategies, solutions, and narratives are credible, competitive, and effective in local markets and with governments.
Within this, the Signals & Localization Readiness team sits at the forefront of anticipating change. The team identifies emerging signals across payments, geopolitics, and technology, translates them into business implications, and enables Mastercard to proactively position for advantage.
Role
This is a high-visibility Manager role at the intersection of analytics, market intelligence, and strategic storytelling.
The role is fundamentally about making sense of a complex, fast-evolving external environment, and shaping how Mastercard understands and responds to it. You will own core strategic products that inform leadership thinking and decision-making.
The role offers a unique opportunity to shape how Mastercard anticipates change, positions itself in markets, and communicates its point of view on the evolving future of payments. Success requires the ability to move fluidly between data, narrative, and judgment: spotting patterns early, structuring ambiguity, and articulating clear implications for the business. This role requires a high degree of ownership across both strategic thinking and execution: taking pride in producing high-quality outputs at every level of detail.
Key Responsibilities
Own Strategic Intelligence Resources
Own and maintain the team's core intelligence resources, ensuring they remain accurate, current, and aligned to evolving market, policy, and industry developments.
Oversee the ongoing curation, quality assurance, and enhancement of key datasets that underpin the team's thought leadership, research, and strategic insights.
Identify emerging trends, gaps, and opportunities within these resources and translate findings into actionable intelligence for stakeholders.
Partner with colleagues across MA to leverage these resources in reports, publications, presentations, and strategic initiatives.
Produce Thought Leadership & Written Insights
Support ongoing signals monitoring by tracking external developments across markets, policy, and competitors
Author high-quality newsletters and insight pieces on the future of payments, geopolitics, and localization trends
Translate complex concepts into clear, structured, and compelling narratives
Help shape Mastercard’s internal perspective on market, regulatory, and ecosystem shifts
Own KPI Dashboards & Reporting
Design, build, and maintain dashboards tracking localization and business performance metrics
Generate insights, ensuring data accuracy, consistency, and clarity for executive audiences
Support Strategy & Execution
Contribute to strategy development, executive presentations, and playbooks
Partner with cross-functional and regional teams to drive initiatives forward
Enable Team Effectiveness & Communications
Support team communications, knowledge management, and content platforms
Improve processes and ways of working with an entrepreneurial mindset
All About You
Quantitative + Storytelling Strength
Excel fluency required
Able to translate data into clear, insightful narratives
Familiarity with Mastercard internal platforms and databases an advantage
Compelling Writer
Proven ability to produce crisp, structured, high-quality written content (e.g., newsletters, reports, briefings)
Strong editorial judgment and attention to detail
Analytical & Curious
Intellectually curious with the ability to connect business, payments innovation, and global/regulatory dynamics
Entrepreneurial & Hands-On
Self-starter who can build from scratch, iterate quickly, and “get hands dirty”
Strong execution mindset in ambiguous environments
Collaborative & Organized
Team-oriented with a strong sense of shared ownership; willing to lean in to ensure team success
High attention to detail and pride in producing accurate, polished work
Comfortable balancing strategic thinking with hands-on execution
Global Mindset
Experience working across markets strongly preferred
English fluency required; additional languages a plus

Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

Title and Summary
Director Legal Compliance
Overview
Mastercard Transaction Services (MTS) enables Mastercard to deliver regulated payment products through licensed entities across multiple jurisdictions.
We are seeking an experienced Financial Crime Compliance professional to lead Compliance governance and oversight of the MTS new product intake process across fiat and digital products.
Reporting to the Global MTS Compliance VP, Governance, Risk and Controls, the Director will provide financial crime compliance oversight and advisory support throughout the product lifecycle, ensuring that new products and material enhancements are appropriately risk assessed, governed and supported by effective compliance controls prior to launch.
The role will work closely with Product, Compliance Technology and Systems, Compliance Operations, Legal, Regulatory Compliance, Finance, Global Compliance and MTS Entity MLRO teams.
Key Responsibilities
Lead Compliance governance and oversight of new product intake across MTS fiat and digital products.
Assess new products and material enhancements to identify inherent AML, sanctions, fraud and other financial crime risks.
Complete and maintain required financial crime risk assessments, providing SME input into entity-level and enterprise-wide risk and control assessments.
Define and maintain the new product intake governance framework, process flow and key controls, driving consistent adoption across products and MTS entities.
Oversee pre- and post-implementation financial crime systems and technical requirements, working with Compliance Systems, Technical Design/Model teams, Compliance Operations and MLRO teams.
Ensure product-related compliance requirements are appropriately reflected across technology, systems, operational controls and policy frameworks.
Provide governance reporting to relevant forums, including the MTS Compliance Committee and MTS Change Initiatives Forum.
Maintain the New Product Intake Register, including the status of Compliance reviews, approvals, exceptions and dispensations, and ensure timely follow-up.
Identify and drive remediation of gaps arising from internal or external issues, events and control assessments to strengthen the overall intake process.
Support the wider MTS GRC team with risk assessments, issue management, reporting and design assurance relating to new product intake.
Lead Compliance coordination across relevant Product, Legal, Finance, Regulatory Compliance, Global Compliance and MTS Entity teams.
Provide Compliance governance and oversight for digital asset and crypto product intake, including VASPs, crypto card programmes, stablecoins such as USDC and PYUSD, Send Crypto, Crypto Credential and other emerging digital payment propositions.
Required Experience and Technical Skills
Compliance experience, ideally within international payments, transactional banking, regulated fintech or a comparable global financial services environment.
Demonstrable experience developing and implementing financial crime controls within new product intake or product approval processes.
Strong understanding of AML, KYC, sanctions, fraud, transaction monitoring and investigation processes there by supporting enterprise wide transformation programmes
Good project management skills.
Strong understanding of how new products impact Compliance operations, technology, systems, controls and policy frameworks.
Experience or strong knowledge of card payments, digital commerce, cross-border payment flows and blockchain analytics.
Strong understanding of crypto compliance and VASP-related risks, ideally within a regulated fintech, payments or crypto-native environment.
Familiarity with advanced and automated compliance systems, including AML, sanctions and fraud alert management. Exposure to the use of AI in Compliance is a distinct advantage.
Experience in process mapping, compliance framework development, control design, process automation and scalable Compliance solutions.
Proven ability to operate in a complex global matrix environment, across multiple jurisdictions, time zones and stakeholders.
Strong communication and influencing skills, with the ability to challenge constructively, influence senior leaders and articulate clear, risk-based recommendations.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, interpersonal and organisational skills.
Holder of a globally recognised Financial Crime Compliance qualification.
Proficient in Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel and Visio.

Our Process Improvement Specialists are always thinking about the bigger picture. Every position at Amazon offers the opportunity for employees to influence business decisions and shape the future. As a Process Improvement Specialist, pioneering new ways of thinking, designing and delivering is your mission. Collaborating with a wide range of stakeholders across the business, you’ll continuously be scoping out new solutions. You’ll conduct your own research and analysis, always with an eye on the long-term vision of the business. This is your opportunity to have a big impact on some of the most exciting new ideas that are shaping the future of Amazon.
Key job responsibilities
Create innovative solutions using data and research to address wider challenges in your organisation
Take a big-picture approach in your analysis of business operations, driving improvements across a range of teams and organisations
Work alongside senior leadership to establish and prioritise improvement programmes, seeing them through from start to finish

A day in the life
As Process Improvement Specialist, you’ll drive and manage the implementation of creative, data-driven change in Amazon, leading improvement projects and programmes. You’ll use strategic thinking to define and implement an efficient project plan.
You’ll deal with complex challenges with creativity, innovation, and leadership. With a responsibility extending beyond process improvements, you could also contribute to improving other areas of the business, like diversity, equity, and inclusion.
About the team
Amazon Extra Large (AMXL) looks after heavy items like furniture and large home appliances. Our team manages the entire service, from supply chain fulfilment to delivery and returns. What sets this service apart from others is the extra level of customer care. Not only do we deliver large items, but we unpack, assemble and install them, and take away old items where needed. With a focus on safety, productivity and innovation, we’re changing the way customers buy and receive large goods for the better.
We have ambitious plans to expand our specialist fulfilment centres and delivery stations across the UK and Europe. While those of us who work in delivery stations will do some night shifts, most of us work during the day. Our team is made up of people across operations, supply chain, business intelligence and programme management, and everyone plays a crucial role in growing this part of the business.

jd.text:
AWS Global Sales drives adoption of the AWS cloud worldwide, enabling customers of all sizes to innovate and expand in the cloud. Our team empowers every customer to grow by providing tailored service, unmatched technology, and unwavering support. We dive deep to understand each customer's unique challenges, then craft innovative solutions that accelerate their success. This customer-first approach is how we built the world's most adopted cloud. Join us and help us grow.
Would you like to lead AWS’s relationships with Private Equity (PE) firms, and influence decision making toward AWS for their portfolio companies’ infrastructure? Do you have the business acumen, technical command, and advisory experience necessary to earn trust within the PE ecosystem and help further establish Amazon as the leader in cloud services?
As a Principal Business Development Manager on the AWS Private Equity team, you have the exciting opportunity to help shape and deliver on a strategy to achieve broader use of AWS within the PE firms and their portfolio companies, with a particular focus on digital transformation. Your responsibilities include identifying and prioritizing PE firms to engage, driving the necessary business, strategic and technical relationships to establish new business in the firms and in their investments. You work closely with AWS sales teams to drive day-to-day interactions with the portfolio companies in order to build long-term business opportunity. You also collaborate with our partner network, AWS corporate development, industry specialists, product management and marketing teams on strategic initiatives that tie in to the PE community.
The ideal candidate possesses both a business background that enables them to lead extended, complex engagements at the CxO/VP level, as well as a technical background that enables them to easily interact with technical leaders, software developers, architects, and data scientists. You demonstrate the ability to think strategically and analytically about business, product, and technical challenges to build and convey compelling value propositions. You work with intentionality, consistently assess impact and work cross-organizationally to build scalable solutions. A strong sense of ownership, initiative, and resourcefulness is essential.
Key job responsibilities
Serve as a key member of the Business Development team in helping drive AWS market and technical strategy.
Identify infrastructure needs within key PE portfolio companies, and drive engagement through the PE firms.
Execute a strategic business development plan, effectively aligning with key internal stakeholders (e.g. sales and account teams, partners, marketing, support, etc.).
Work closely with PE firms and portfolio company leadership to ensure they derive optimized benefit from our web services, and have access to the technical resources required.
Understand and actively utilize Analytics tools and other internal Amazon systems.
Prepare and give business reviews to AWS senior leadership regarding progress and roadblocks in establishing PE engagement.
Serve as the primary eyes and ears to the PE community on behalf of AWS and Amazon.
Handle a high volume of concurrent engagements and scale with the fast pace of GenAI and cloud computing
Some relevant business level technical knowledge is required, such as: database systems, core distributed computing concepts, fundamentals of cloud computing and virtualization, storage systems, GenAI and machine learning, content delivery networks (CDNs) etc. with ability to go deep enough on technical aspects to differentiate between core AWS services.
About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.
Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.
Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

records.title: Network Planning Manager, MMNC - Middle Mile Network Control

jd.text:
This role tagged as one of Amazon’s Supply Chain Managers play a central role in our global business. They keep our complex, international supply chains working seamlessly and efficiently. As a Supply Chain Manager (SCM), you will work closely with multiple stakeholders across Amazon, from Operational teams who are fulfilling customer orders to Retail teams and everything in between. You’ll help us optimise our supply chains to make our customer experience even better and our business more energy and cost efficient.
Key job responsibilities
Define the Amazon outbound network planning (Legs, Sorts, CPT) for one of the UK sub-regions covered by 3-5 Sort Centers.
Analyse the best design based on forecast, and historical flows to improve cost, speed and DEA across E2E network.
Partner with teams to align on network changes to solve operational challenges.
Support the planning and organization of complex projects including Peak network transformations
A day in the life
Being a Network Manager for Amazon involves lots of problem solving. You’ll work with a number of teams to navigate challenges as and when situations impact our network. You’ll spend time resolving temporary issues and looking at the bigger picture to drive Amazon towards achieving new objectives. This role is both proactive and reactive, and you’ll have the opportunity to help forecast and plan for new projects.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.
We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. Our work spans Payments, Business Accounts, Spend and APIs, combining deep product expertise with a highly consultative, customer-first approach.
This is an opportunity to join the founding team of our EMEA Enterprise Customer Success function. You will work closely with our existing Customer Success Manager and help shape the processes, playbooks and operating model for the team as it grows.
Our UK team is growing and currently has more than 110 employees. We operate in a hybrid environment, with three days per week required in our London office at Wells & More, Fitzrovia.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
As an Enterprise Customer Success Manager, you will own the post-sale relationship for a portfolio of strategic customers. You will partner with customers throughout implementation, go-live and ongoing growth, ensuring they achieve measurable value from Airwallex.
You will work cross-functionally with Sales, Account Management, Solutions Engineering, Product, Support, Operations, Billing and Technical teams to deliver exceptional customer outcomes.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Act as a founding member of the EMEA Enterprise Customer Success team and help build the function from the ground up.
Manage and grow relationships with embedded finance customers and enterprise clients, typically organisations with more than 1,000 employees.
Own the customer lifecycle from implementation and go-live through adoption, expansion and renewal.
Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, technical teams and operational contacts across customer organisations.
Lead complex implementation and onboarding programmes, coordinating internal and external stakeholders to deliver against agreed timelines.
Develop customer success plans, define objectives and establish success metrics aligned to each customer’s business goals.
Serve as the primary escalation point for operational, technical and service-related issues.
Coordinate with Sales, Account Management, Support, Billing, Product and Engineering to drive timely resolution of customer issues.
Monitor product adoption, transaction volumes, service levels, failure rates and other key performance indicators.
Use data and customer insights to identify risks, recommend improvements and drive increased adoption and value.
Support customers in optimising their use of Airwallex’s APIs, Payments, Business Accounts and Spend solutions.
Project-manage the rollout of new products, features and capabilities across your accounts.
Proactively identify opportunities to improve the customer experience and prevent potential issues.
Ensure customers receive clear, timely and proactive communication throughout incidents, changes and key delivery milestones.
Develop deep expertise in Airwallex’s products and embedded finance capabilities to advise customers and resolve complex challenges.
Contribute to the development of scalable playbooks, processes and best practices for Enterprise Customer Success.
WHO YOU ARE
You have 5+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Solutions Delivery, Operations or a related client-facing role supporting enterprise customers.
You have experience working with complex organisations, multiple stakeholders and long implementation cycles.
Experience in fintech, payments, banking, APIs or embedded finance is highly desirable.
You are an accomplished relationship builder who can establish credibility and trust with stakeholders at all levels of seniority.
You have exceptional communication and presentation skills and are comfortable engaging with both technical and non-technical audiences.
You are commercially minded and able to identify opportunities to drive customer value, adoption and growth.
You are highly organised and comfortable managing multiple complex projects and priorities simultaneously.
You are detail-oriented and understand the importance of operational accuracy when supporting enterprise customers.
You are technically minded and have experience delivering, implementing or troubleshooting SaaS, API-based or other technical solutions.
You are proactive, solutions-oriented and comfortable working in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
You enjoy building from scratch and are excited by the opportunity to help shape a new Customer Success function.

Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv.
We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.
Job Title
Senior Project Manager
About your role:
Reporting to the Program Director, the role of Senior Project Manager is to scope, plan and deliver projects and initiatives to meet specified business needs, controlling resources from several areas (and potentially third parties) to achieve agreed cost, time and quality objectives.
The Senior Project Manager has the overall accountability and responsibility for the progress and successful delivery of the project effort.
What you’ll do:
Defining the project brief
Setting client expectations in respect of deliverables, plans and management of the project
Establishing an appropriate project governance structure, in line with the Fiserv programme/project methodology /governance
Assisting the Client and Sponsor to obtain authorisations and signoffs on the Business Case
Documenting the overall project approach, including the phasing strategy
Developing estimates of resources, costs and durations and based on these, creating a high-level project schedule and requesting appropriate resources
Facilitating the development of all elements of the project plans and schedule according to the project brief, i.e. plans for scope, schedule, budget, change management, issues, risk, procurement, testing, training, communication and transition to BAU. Agree plans with all relevant stakeholders
Ensuring that any impacts of the project on business processes and business continuity are assessed and continually monitored as the project develops
Execution & Controls
Managing, maintaining and tracking the overall project plan, controls, budget and work assignments according to established Fiserv governance
Reporting project status (schedule, cost, benefit, risk, issues and scope) to all stakeholders on a regular basis
Organising and facilitating appropriate level of governance meetings, to discuss status reports, provide structured escalation path and determine corrective or preventive actions
Managing project risks and issues, ensuring that project team members are actively involved in the identification and where appropriate the ownership of risks, initiating corrective action where necessary
Ensuring that project team members are accurately recording their time spent on project tasks and thus tracking budget accurately
Building and maintaining a cohesive cross organisation/company project team ethos and fostering productive working relationships, optimally assigning tasks to team members
Ensuring the development and approval of all deliverables
Refining resource, cost and duration estimate as the project progresses, ensuring that requests for resources for each phase are supplied sufficiently early to enable them to be secured when needed
Managing proposed changes in scope, schedule or budget with key stakeholders relaying any impact to cost, schedule or scope and providing a recommended course of action.
Scheduling, managing and participating in key quality reviews and developing action plans to resolve issues arising
Organising, leading, and motivating a matrix team of Fiserv SME’s and potentially 3rd party resources
Maintaining a dialogue with PMO to ensure that defined project processes are followed and that any issues are resolved in a timely manner
Ensuring a clean, structured and fully supported transition to BAU
Providing out of hours cover over implementation weekends when Project goes live
Project administration
Closeout & Transition
Obtaining approval from the sponsor that the acceptance criteria have been met
Confirming that the project’s objectives have been achieved
Confirming that all outstanding risks and issues have been accepted by the sponsor
Performing comparisons of estimated and actual costs and completing financial closeout
Facilitating the project evaluation and obtaining approval to close out the project, documented within end project report
Performing contract and project closeout activities, and archiving project information. Where applicable conducting a formal Lessons Learned session and publishing results to all stakeholders
Experience you’ll need to have:
Expert in MSOffice Products especially WORD, EXCEL, PowerPoint and MS-Project
In-depth understanding of business processes within Client portfolio
Ability to plan and monitor an entire programme consisting of multiple endpoints
Educated to degree-level in Computer Science, Business, Accounting, Marketing or equivalent work experience
Excellent verbal and written communications skills in Italian/English proficiency
History of matrix-managing others for the successful completion of a medium to large projects. Having managed full lifecycle projects with inter-dependent or direct resources
Experience that would be great to have:
Significant proven Project Management experience preferably gained within the Finance industry
Salary starting at €67,500 - negotiable depending on experience
Thank you for considering employment with Fiserv. Please:
Apply using your legal name
Complete the step-by-step profile and attach your resume (either is acceptable, both are preferable).
Our commitment to Diversity and Inclusion:
Fiserv is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other category protected by law.
Note to agencies:
Fiserv does not accept resume submissions from agencies outside of existing agreements. Please do not send resumes to Fiserv associates. Fiserv is not responsible for any fees associated with unsolicited resume submissions.

Please be aware of fraudulent job postings that are not affiliated with Fiserv. Any communications from a Fiserv representative will come from a legitimate Fiserv email address.

Role – Head of Data Protection
Who are we?
Howden is a collective – a group of talented and passionate people all around the world. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mind-set, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 100 countries.
Our people are our biggest asset as well as our largest shareholder group and are everything that makes us unique; our inclusive culture, the quality service we offer our clients, and our continued growth, all come from our people-first approach. There’s no such thing as individual success. We all need to play our part, contributing our skills and experience to make a true difference. That’s Howden.
Why work at Howden?
We have always been employee-owned and driven by entrepreneurial spirit. Right from the beginning, we've focused on employing talented individuals and empowering them to make a real difference to the company, whilst building successful and fulfilling careers at the same time. Simply put, we hire talented specialists and give them what they need to make a difference for clients. Always have, always will.
People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down disappointed head-hunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work/life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.
What is the role?
Head of Data Protection Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance shall lead the Data Protection Function that is responsible for developing, implementing, embedding and maintaining a data protection control and oversight framework for Howden’s UK Broking (including its Specialty and Retail Pillars) and UK Reinsurance Divisions. The framework must be pragmatic, risk based and suitably robust to support Howden’s UK Broking and UK Reinsurance entities to meet applicable data protection legislation, including the UK Data Protection Act, but also any other applicable legislation in territories where those entities operate. The framework must also align to and complement Howden Group’s overarching Data Protection framework, governance and policy.
What will you be doing?
Oversight & Change
Work closely with Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance senior leadership to develop and drive a data protection strategy that is aligned to the operating model and strategies of those businesses, promoting and supporting consistency of approach and application as much as practically possible.
Develop and maintain an annual Data Protection Plan setting out the resources needed to deliver the projects and activities to be undertaken by the function, which shall be aligned to and support the regulatory expectations and objectives of the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses (which may include their overseas operations).
Support in developing and maintaining a data protection risk and control framework, including data protection policy, processes, procedures, controls and monitoring.
Implementing a data protection horizon scanning process, ensuring any new or changing legislation is identified and implemented by expected timeframes.
Produce reports and escalate data protection updates, risks, issues and compliance performance to the relevant Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance governance committees.
Establish and maintain an effective data protection risk identification and escalation process across all Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses, ensuring swift and timely mitigation or management of risks and breaches.
Develop, maintain and promote the consistent use of data protection tooling.
Continually raise awareness of data protection and ensure adequate programme of data protection related training to employees.
Oversee and manage any reporting to and interaction with data protection supervisory authorities, including the Information Commissioner’s Office.
Ensure that all Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses have the correct data protection registrations and licences.
Support in embedding a data protection by design approach within Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses.
Stakeholders
Develop and maintain appropriate working relationships with the following to ensure that data protection issues are identified and proactive provision of appropriate solutions:
Key senior leadership across the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses to ensure a strong understanding of their current and future strategies, business models and objectives, to proactively pre-empt and recognise the data protection support they will require.
Key operational and functional heads that are responsible for the development and delivery of operational processes and systems to embed a data protection by design approach and to support swift escalation of risks and concerns.
Key information security leadership and functions, to ensure a clear understanding of information security processes and controls, and how these dovetail and work alongside data protection controls and risk mitigants.
Internal Control Function Heads across the first, second and third line of defence, to develop an aligned and complementary risk, control and assurance framework, and to support addressing remedial actions.
Group Head of Data Protection and wider group data protection functions to support an alignment of approach, ensure consistent upward escalation and reporting and to share best practice and common risks and issues.
Function responsibilities
To develop, support and maintain a data protection function that is able to achieve the following for Howden’s UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses.
Providing timely and considered advice and guidance on a range of data protection matters relating to Howden’s UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses, this will include, but will not be limited to – Marketing, DPIA’s, Subject Rights, Privacy Notices, Data Security.
Supporting compliance with the UK Data Protection Act, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), other Data Protection Laws and the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR).
Establish processes to monitoring compliance with the EU GDPR and other data protection laws, such as the UK Data Protection Act 2018, our data protection policies, including internal data protection activities, raising awareness of data protection issues, training staff;
Providing advice on the conduct of and supervising data protection impact assessments (DPIAs);
Completing a Record of Processing Activities (ROPA) that cover each of the in scope entities within Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance.
Complete annual Data Protection Risk Assessments for Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance, ensuring that these are reported to the relevant governing committees, but that they also support and contribute to wider Howden Group Data Protection Risk Assessments and ERICCA.
Support in the development and on-going reporting of KRI and KCIs that feed into the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance risk management framework and, where relevant, Howden Group risk management framework and ERICCA.
Having regard to the risk associated with processing operations and taking account of the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing
Prioritising focus on the more risky activities, e.g. where special category (sensitive) personal data is processed, or where the potential impact on individuals could be damaging;
Establishing clear points of contact for all BAU data protection queries from Howden’s UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses with regard to potential complaints and breaches, ensuring that data subject rights’ requests accurately handled
Making available data protection resources, policies, procedures, guidance, training material and points of contact information in a way that is easily accessible.
Team management
Develop and maintain a function with the appropriate blend of skill, experience and knowledge to deliver the data protection support and oversight required by the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses.
Implement an approach to employee development which enables employees to enhance their data protection, industry and Howden knowledge, experience and skill set.
Provides visionary leadership by fostering a culture of employee engagement and role modelling, encouraging and rewarding essential behaviours and maintaining a high level of personal and professional confidence
Manages (resource, motivate, drive, develop and focus) the team to ensure the required standards of performance are met; and that the professional and personal development of all team members increases their capability and effectiveness
Promotes individual accountability through an ongoing performance management approach that aligns personal performance goals with the functional and wider business goals
Ensures there are effective succession plans in place and actively develops team members to provide future successors
Identifies and hires talent
Manage (resource, motivate, drive, develop and focus) the UK data Protection Function to ensure the required standards of performance are met; and that the professional and personal development of all team members increases their capability and effectiveness
Actively undertakes personal development to ensure up to date knowledge and understanding of best practice
Develop and maintain appropriate working relationships with the following to ensure that data protection issues are identified and proactive provision of appropriate solutions:
Key senior leadership across the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses to ensure a strong understanding of their current and future strategies, business models and objectives, to proactively pre-empt and recognise the data protection support they will require.
Key operational and functional heads that are responsible for the development and delivery of operational processes and systems to embed a data protection by design approach and to support swift escalation of risks and concerns.
Key information security leadership and functions, to ensure a clear understanding of information security processes and controls, and how these dovetail and work alongside data protection controls and risk mitigants.
Internal Control Function Heads across the first, second and third line of defence, to develop an aligned and complementary risk, control and assurance framework, and to support addressing remedial actions.
Group Head of Data Protection and wider group data protection functions to support an alignment of approach, ensure consistent upward escalation and reporting and to share best practice and common risks and issues.
What are we looking for?
Ability to provide risk-based advice.
Experience in achieving stated objectives involving a diverse set of business partners and leading multifaceted projects.
Negotiation skills to work effectively with key internal and external partners.
Client relationship skills to continuously coordinate with controllers and processors while maintaining independence.
Interpersonal skills to communicate well with a wide-ranging audience, from the Board of Directors to data subjects, from managers to IT staff and lawyers.
Self-starter with ability to gain required knowledge in wide-ranging environments.
Experienced within a Data Protection compliance field, to include building, implementing and managing data protection programmes within a sophisticated and enterprise-wide organisation.
Experience with supporting marketing initiatives and the PECR regulations.
Experience in handling data subject rights requests.
Detailed knowledge of UK and European data protection law, and an in-depth knowledge of the GDPR.
An understanding of technical and operational measures that should be in place to ensure the security of personal data and familiarity with information technologies and data security.
Experience in compliance monitoring and risk management.
Experienced in producing and presenting data protection reports to senior governance committees.
Experienced in developing and delivering data protection training to employees of all levels.
Financial Services experience preferred.
Compliance & Regulatory Responsibilities
Compliance with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), UK Data Protection Act 2018, other UK data protection / privacy related legislation (such as the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations) and ICO guidance related to the tasks of a DPO.
Professional Qualifications
CIPP/E or Certified Data Protection Practitioner (PC.dp) preferred but not essential
What do we offer in return?
A career that you define.
Our business succeeds by allowing our people to make a mark in the areas they care about most: personal development, volunteering, and fundraising for charity, or creating new insurance products that address society’s greatest challenges.
And we know that separate home and work lives don't really exist. If you're happy and healthy at home, you're more likely to be happy and fulfilled at work – and vice versa. That's why we do our best to support our people in every aspect of their lives.
Diversity and Inclusion
At Howden we value diversity - there is no one Howden ‘personality type’. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new
We support each other, in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges
We are determined to make a positive difference, at work and beyond
We consider our people our chief competitive advantage and as such we treat colleagues, candidates, clients, and business partners with equality, fairness, and respect – regardless of age, disability, race, religion or belief, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, or family circumstances.
Our sustainability promise
We’re on a life-long journey to become an ever-more sustainable group. It's a commitment to taking care of our people and the world we live in, to doing good business, and to making a positive impact wherever we can. Our governance processes, company policies, and review systems are all geared towards our goal of making a positive impact in the world. You can read more about our sustainability work here .
What do we offer in return?
A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new
We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges
We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond
Reasonable adjustments
We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations at Howden to ensure that our positions align well with your needs. Besides the usual adjustments such as software, IT, and office setups, we can also accommodate other changes such as flexible hours* or hybrid working*.
If you're excited by this role but have some doubts about whether it’s the right fit for you, send us your application – if your profile fits the role’s criteria, we will be in touch to assist in helping to get you set up with any reasonable adjustments you may require.
*Not all positions can accommodate changes to working hours or locations. Reach out to your Recruitment Partner if you want to know more.
Permanent

Activities:
We are looking for an experienced Finance Change & Transformation Expert to design and deliver change initiatives across Accounting, Financial Reporting and Regulatory Reporting, covering both Group and local requirements. Working across Finance, Business, Risk, Operations, Data and Technology, the role translates accounting and regulatory needs into sustainable processes, governed data flows and system solutions, supporting the progressive and responsible adoption of AI in Finance through prioritized use cases, controlled experimentation and evidence-based scaling.
The successful candidate will combine Finance and Reporting expertise with business analysis, project management and change execution capabilities, supported by sound Data Management and AI literacy. Key initiatives may include new accounting standards, evolving Group and local reporting frameworks, process optimization, data governance and quality improvements, and a phased AI adoption roadmap—from low-risk pilots and quick wins to broader deployment once value, controls and operational readiness are demonstrated— as well as core banking or Finance system transformations.
Responsibilities:
Lead end-to-end Finance change and transformation initiatives, from impact assessment and target solution design through implementation and post-go-live stabilization.
Support Group and local subject-matter experts in assessing the impact of new or amended accounting standards, regulatory requirements and business products on accounting treatments, processes, controls, data, systems and reporting, including Data Management implications and the readiness of Finance processes for gradual AI adoption.
Translate Group and local Finance needs into clear business and functional requirements, process designs, data specifications, data-quality, lineage and ownership requirements, and acceptance criteria.
Design and implement accounting, Financial Reporting and Regulatory Reporting solutions, introducing analytics, automation and approved AI capabilities progressively: identify and prioritize use cases, run controlled pilots, measure outcomes and scale proven solutions.
Coordinate cross-functional workstreams across Finance, Risk, Compliance, Operations, Data and Technology, involving Group and local stakeholders.
Define project scope, plans, milestones, dependencies, resources and governance; monitor delivery, risks, issues and remediation actions, and prepare concise decision papers and steering updates.
Plan and coordinate functional and user acceptance testing, data migration, accounting reconciliation and reporting validation, including controls over data quality and, where relevant, AI output accuracy, explainability and human oversight.
Ensure solutions are compliant, scalable, properly controlled and supported by clear audit trails and documentation, with appropriate data and AI governance, privacy, security and model-risk safeguards.
Drive process simplification, standardization and automation while safeguarding the integrity, accuracy and timeliness of financial and regulatory information.
Support stakeholder engagement, training, business readiness and transition to business-as-usual operations.
Required skills:
Master’s degree in Economics, Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Management Engineering or a related discipline.
At least four years of audit experience, preferably with banks or other regulated financial institutions, followed by consulting or Finance transformation experience as a business or functional analyst, project manager or workstream lead (2 years minimum).
Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial statements and end-to-end Finance processes; knowledge of banking products and related accounting flows is highly desirable.
Proven involvement in complex Finance initiatives, such as IFRS 9, IFRS 16 or IFRS 18 implementation, general ledger transformation, Finance data architecture, Data Management or AI-enabled process transformation, or core banking implementation.
Understanding of bank prudential and supervisory reporting requirements and their linkage to source data, calculations, controls and reporting outputs, together with working knowledge of data governance, quality and lineage principles.
Hands-on experience in requirements gathering, process mapping, impact analysis, solution design, testing, migration, reconciliation and implementation.
Sound project management skills and familiarity with traditional and Agile delivery approaches, plus the ability to shape a pragmatic Finance AI roadmap, prioritize viable use cases, assess value and risks, and coordinate pilots and subsequent scaling with Data, Analytics, Technology and control functions.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, attention to detail and a pragmatic, delivery-oriented mindset.
Excellent stakeholder management, facilitation and communication skills, including interaction with senior management and international stakeholders.
Ability to work effectively across functions and geographies, managing ambiguity and multiple priorities.
Fluent written and spoken English.
Key competencies:
Finance expertise and business acumen
Change leadership and delivery focus
Structured analysis and problem solving
Stakeholder influence and cross-functional collaboration
Risk awareness, control mindset and auditability, including responsible Data and AI use
Data fluency and a pragmatic, progressive AI adoption mindset
Clear and concise communication

Our compensation approach is built on objective, gender-neutral criteria aligned with the role’s core requirements. That said, we believe talent goes beyond any framework: your total reward package will be tailored to reflect your unique experience, skills, and potential, ensuring we fully recognize the value you bring.
The benefits of joining ING
In addition to being a part of a great team, working in a fun and innovative environment, we offer:
Flexible Smart Working

A special day off when it is your birthday: we call it #doyourbirthday!
And of course, we can’t forget free water & coffee at the office!
About ING
ING offers many opportunities to build a diverse and rewarding career. You will be joining an international innovative digital bank, the first in Italy to adopt a fully flexible smart working model, and you will be working in a stimulating environment where you can grow both as an individual and as a professional.
Our purpose - empowering people to stay a step ahead in life and in business - represents our belief in people’s potential. We don’t judge, coach or to tell people how to live their lives. We empower people and businesses to realize their own vision for a better future.
Our Commitment
Diversity is a fundamental element of our corporate culture, and we are fully committed to creating a safe and inclusive environment, based on mutual respect and the value of diversity, offering equal job opportunities to all qualified candidates.
Job Application Safety Reminder ⚠️
We’re seeing an increase in fraudulent job offers. To protect yourself, please follow these key guidelines when applying for roles at ING:
· Apply only via official ING platforms: ING uses Workday as its internal recruitment system. Applications should be submitted only via our official career site.
· Check the sender’s email carefully: legitimate communication will always come from: @ing.com and/or @myworkday.com
· No payments or banking details will ever be requested. If someone asks for this information, it’s a scam.
If you suspect suspicious activity, report it immediately. Your safety matters to us.

About us
Traditional banking has never really given you control over your financial life. Satispay exists to change that: to empower people through finance.
That means making financial services easy and accessible for over 6.5M users. We started with payments, then benefits, investing, cards... and we’re not done. Not even close.
We follow the same logic every time: find a real problem, solve it properly, then look for the next one. The destination? To build the most loved financial platform in the world.
If you own outcomes rather than tasks, stay close to what users need, and refuse to wait for someone else to fix what's broken — you'll find people here who work exactly in the same way. And together, you'll build something worth being proud of.
What you'll be doing
As our Procurement Specialist, you'll implement integrated procurement strategies to support company objectives, manage procurement cost records, ensure departments follow correct procurement flows, optimize buying activities, and continuously monitor key procurement metrics.
Here's what that looks like in practice:
Lead vendor negotiations and manage procurement spend - Negotiate with suppliers to secure optimal terms, maximize value, and monitor pricing dynamics and market trends.
Support internal stakeholders - Partner with business teams to provide procurement guidance and ensure consistency with company policies.

records.title: Junior Commercial Associate — Works in Progress

jd.text:
Location: London, in office Reports to: Head of Commercial and Audiovisual, Works in Progress Salary: £30k-35k
About Works in Progress
Works in Progress is Stripe’s magazine of new and underrated ideas to improve the world. We publish an eclectic mix of articles on policy, economics, business, technology, science, history, arts and culture.
Our audience is growing quickly and includes people making things happen, particularly in technology and politics. We are expanding the commercial side of the magazine—including advertising, subscriptions, events and partnerships—and are looking for an ambitious graduate to help us build it.
The role
This is an entry-level commercial role for a recent graduate who is ambitious, organised and excited to learn quickly in a small, entrepreneurial team.
You will work closely with the Director of Commercial and Audiovisual across the magazine’s commercial activity: advertising, subscriptions, events, marketing and partnerships. You will help keep commercial projects moving by conducting research, supporting outreach, maintaining pipelines and trackers, following up with prospective partners, and contributing to growth experiments.
You will learn by doing: writing outbound emails, building target lists, preparing materials, tracking results, joining calls and following up consistently. It is a strong opportunity for someone who wants early exposure to senior commercial work and meaningful responsibility from the start of their career.
What you’ll do
Support the advertising sales process, including preparing rate cards, pitch decks, outreach and pipeline materials.
Research and build target lists of potential advertisers, sponsors, agencies, founders, investors and partners.
Draft clear, thoughtful outbound emails and follow-ups.
Maintain accurate CRM records, commercial trackers and reporting.
Support subscription growth through acquisition and retention ideas, and help measure their effectiveness.
Help develop the events business, including sponsor research, partnership outreach and event planning support.
Assist with early marketing and growth experiments across paid acquisition, referrals, partnerships, direct mail and audience development.
Prepare decks, reports and briefing materials that help commercial conversations move forward.
Join meetings and calls with clients, partners and agencies, taking notes and supporting follow-up.
Help turn commercial ideas into clear proposals with pricing, positioning and next steps.
Work across sales, marketing, events and subscriptions, adapting quickly as priorities evolve.
Take on the practical, sometimes unglamorous work needed to help a small business grow.
We’re looking for someone who
Is a recent graduate, or has equivalent early-career experience.
Is excited by commercial work and motivated by helping ideas turn into revenue.
Is interested in sales, marketing, partnerships, media, events or business development.
Is highly organised and comfortable managing lists, trackers and multiple follow-ups.
Is numerate and confident using spreadsheets.
Is a sharp, clear writer who can communicate professionally over email and in presentations.
Is proactive, resilient and comfortable reaching out to people they do not know.
Is curious, resourceful and willing to learn quickly.
Enjoys working in a small team where everyone pitches in.
Is comfortable with both high-profile opportunities and repetitive operational work, such as researching prospects and following up on outreach.
Has an interest in media, publishing, technology, economics, policy or culture. Previous media or publishing experience is helpful but not required.
Working at Works in Progress
This role is based in London and requires working from the office every day. You will be part of a small, ambitious team that cares deeply about the magazine and its growth. In return, you will get a steep learning curve, close mentorship and the chance to contribute directly to building the commercial future of Works in Progress.

Senior Project Manager
Are you passionate about translating strategy into measurable business impact? Join Swiss Re’s Client Data Management team within Life & Health Reinsurance, where you will collaborate with senior leaders and cross-functional teams across all regions to shape and deliver the next phase of our global client data agenda.
About the Role
As Senior Project Manager, you will have the overall responsibility for project delivery across the global Client Data Management agenda, from strategic framing through execution, change adoption and benefits realization.
Working closely with senior business sponsors, you will translate strategic direction and business priorities into executable plans, mobilize and engage cross-functional teams, manage dependencies and risks, and drive timely decisions.
This is hands-on delivery role where success means creating momentum, driving accountability and turning plans into outcomes. You will be equally comfortable setting the approach and driving the detail from facilitating senior-management discussions and governance forums to working directly with regional/functional teams to resolve issues and unblock delivery.
Current focus
Client data is increasingly important to decision-making and value creation across Life & Health Reinsurance providing a critical foundation for data-driven and AI-enabled capabilities. With strong foundations established, the focus is now on scaling our client data capabilities to meet growing demand for timely, trusted and reusable data.
In this role, you will be responsible for:
Project leadership: Translate strategic priorities into clear project scope, milestones, delivery plans and measurable outcomes. Provide overall delivery oversight across interdependent workstreams and regions.
Planning and prioritisation: Establish structured approaches to prioritisation and delivery planning including resource and capacity requirements.
Cross-functional delivery: Mobilize and coordinate business and technology delivery across the Life & Health value chain, actively managing dependencies, risks and issues to drive agreed outcomes.
Stakeholder management and governance: Partner closely with project sponsors, functional leaders and senior stakeholders to maintain alignment and enable timely decisions. Provide concise, decision-ready reporting on progress, risks, trade-offs and areas requiring management intervention.
Transformation and change: Drive the evolution of client data processes, governance, accountabilities and ways of working, translating future-state direction into practical change and implementation plans.
Resource and financial management: Work with functional and regional leaders to identify capacity and capability requirements, support resource and funding requests, and manage project financials.
About the Team
The Client Data Management team within Life & Health Reinsurance is a global team responsible for ensuring client data is acquired, validated, ingested and made available across the business. Our mission is to deliver trusted and timely client data that enables confident decisions and sustainable value for Life & Health.
About You
You combine strategic thinking with pragmatic execution, bringing structure and clarity to ambiguity while constructively challenging assumptions and influencing stakeholders across a global organization to drive outcomes.
You adapt your communication and leadership style across different audiences — from delivery teams to senior executives.
Required Experience:
7+ years of experience leading projects and change initiatives, preferably within (Re)insurance.
Strong end-to-end project management experience across business and technology, including planning, governance, risk and dependency management, resource planning and financial management.
Proven ability to translate strategic direction into execution, including shaping the approach where the path forward is not fully defined.
Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, working across functions, regions and seniority levels in a complex global organization.
Experience delivering data and business transformation, including organizational and operating model design and implementation.
Nice to have:
Experience in Life & Health (Re)insurance.
Experience with client data or data-driven business initiatives.
Project and change management certifications (e.g. PMP, PROSCI, Scrum)
For London, the base salary range for this position is between GBP 84'000 and GBP 126'000 for a full-time role. The specific salary offered considers:
the requirements, scope, complexity and responsibilities of the role,
the applicant's own profile including education/qualifications, expertise, specialisation, skills and experience.
In addition to your base salary, Swiss Re offers an attractive performance-based variable compensation component, designed to recognise your achievements. Further you will enjoy a variety of global and location specific benefits.
Eligibility may vary depending on the terms of Swiss Re policies and your employment contract.
About Swiss Re
Swiss Re is one of the world’s leading providers of reinsurance, insurance and other forms of insurance-based risk transfer, working to make the world more resilient. We anticipate and manage a wide variety of risks, from natural catastrophes and climate change to cybercrime. We cover both Property & Casualty and Life & Health. Combining experience with creative thinking and cutting-edge expertise, we create new opportunities and solutions for our clients. This is possible thanks to the collaboration of more than 15,000 employees across the world.
Our success depends on our ability to build an inclusive culture encouraging fresh perspectives and innovative thinking. We embrace a workplace where everyone has equal opportunities to thrive and develop professionally regardless of their age, gender, race, ethnicity, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, skillset, thought or other characteristics. In our inclusive and flexible environment everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and their passion for sustainability.
If you are an experienced professional returning to the workforce after a career break, we encourage you to apply for open positions that match your skills and experience.
We may use AI-powered tools to support the review and evaluation of applications for this position. These tools provide additional insights to our recruitment teams, but all hiring decisions are carefully reviewed and made by people. To learn more about how we use AI in recruitment and how we handle your personal data, please review our Data Privacy Statement before applying.

About Us
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.
At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.
Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.
Job Description
Overview:
What it's all about:
Visa Commercial Solutions (VCS) team creates and delivers products to Visa’s Commercial clients. VCS provides an opportunity for Visa to diversify revenue with differentiated products that deepen customer relationships and deliver innovation across networks. VCS has ambitious growth plans, with the expectation to more than double the business over the next five years. A key part of this growth will come from small businesses, where we will accelerate growth in new, untapped or high opportunity areas.
Based in the Visa Europe hub, this role is a critical component to future growth. You will join the Small Business team within Visa Commercial Solutions (VCS), focused on accelerating SMB revenue and strengthening Visa’s SMB solutions with existing clients. This role will be responsible for ensuring our signed and live partners achieve their growth aspirations alongside Visa as a strategic partner. You will partner with account executives across European markets focused on a defined list of large and high growth clients across both tier 1 Banks and Fintechs. You will bring the best of Visa’s products, know-how and best practice to maximise their launch and enable them to scale.
In addition to deep payments knowledge, the successful applicant will be strategic, creative and commercial whilst demonstrating strong leadership skills.
Travel for client meetings and industry events will be required.
Key Responsibilities:
Provide first and second level support across a defined group of existing clients, building strong relationships and supporting the clients to launch and scale the Visa card programs.
Represent the SMB team at regular client reviews, tracking business performance and advising on opportunities to scale the business.
Partner across the Visa business, in particular with Visa Consulting and Analytics to bring the optimal support to our clients in order to deliver material new spend in the programmes
Conduct research, market mapping, and opportunity sizing to identify areas where Visa can add differentiated value
Be a deep subject-matter expert on the SMB segment, closely tracking industry trends, competing solutions and advising on the next generation of SMB payment solutions.
Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.
Qualifications
Strong understanding of the SMB ecosystem, including the roles of banks, financial institutions, software platforms and B2B payments providers.
Knowledge of relevant SMB payment solutions, including virtual cards, accounts payable and receivable solutions, and APIs.
Experience in a relationship management, product, solutioning, commercial role serving SMB clients.
Excellent relationship-building and influencing skills, with credibility across clients, partners, cross-functional teams and senior leaders.
Strong problem-solving skills, commercial judgement, self-direction and accountability.
Collaborative mindset and a strong track record of effective cross-functional working.
Experience leading and developing high-performing teams across a matrix organisation.
Fluent English; another European language is advantageous.
Visa is an EEO Employer
Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.
